newsitem.title: USA: El Paso Energy enters Brazilian venture.
newsitem.headline: El Paso Energy enters Brazilian venture.

text.p: El Paso Energy Corp said on Wednesday it has signed a joint development agreement to build a 450 megawatt gas-fired power plant in the Macae region of Brazil.
El Paso signed the agreement with Furnas Centrais Eletricas SA, Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd's Brazilian unit, Centrais Electricas Brasileiras SA (Electrobras), and BG Plc's British Gas of Brazil.
The cost of the project is estimated to be more than US$200 million, a company spokesman said.

The power plant is one of the first to be fueled by natural gas in the country and will include a 21.7 mile (35 km) electrical transmission line which will tie into Brazil's interconnected electric system, El Paso said in a statement.
Construction is expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 1997 with initial operations in 1999 and full commercial operations in 2000, El Paso said in a statement.
Furnas, a subsidiary of Electrobras, is the largest generator and transmitter of electric energy in the southeast and midwest of Brazil holds a 10 percent stake in the project.
The other four partners equally own the remaining 90 percent of the project, El Paso said.

Earlier this month, El Paso was named the low bidder on a project to build, own and operate a 150 megawatt power plant in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul in Western Brazil. The final cost of the project is not yet complete.
